alignments.note: Vocative noun together with the subject pronoun the ASV supplies for the following verbless clause, which writes no subject of its own and denotes the same referent; both realizations are this noun's one discontinuous unit, headed on the word writing its lexeme (rule 25). Rule 25 forbids giving the pronoun to מַעֲבִרִים, since a participle in a verbless clause takes only the copula, and rule 36 refuses to mark a vocative's supplied ye added. The competing reading marks it added on the ground that a vocative is an address rather than a subject the ASV resumes; what rule 25 asks is that the verse write the referent earlier, and here it does.
Dummy subject of the recast clause; not a presentative frame and no morpheme licenses it (rule 20).
The clause's negation recast as the determiner no (rule 15).
Predicate adjective with the construction-supplied copula (rule 20), discontinuous around the negation.
The one written determiner is the negative's, so the article has nothing (rules 41 and 29).
Explicit pronoun takes only its own word (rule 20).

Causative participle rendered make ... to transgress; head on the complement verb (rule 44), discontinuous around the object. Its English subject pronoun is the vocative's under rule 25, since a participle in a verbless clause takes only the copula.
The chain's relation is written inside the English possessive (rule 19).

review_notes: Corrected in reconciliation: the supplied ye at t013 is the second realization of the vocative בָּנַי under rule 25 rather than an added word, which is how 1SA.2.6 and 1SA.2.7 read the supplied He beside a written יְהוָה. The verse pass had reached for rule 36's adjacency test, which allocates a ye between an imperative and a vocative standing in one clause; no imperative stands here, and rule 36's first sentence says a vocative's supplied ye is never added.

The pronoun is still not the participle's: rule 25 states that rule 17's permission reaches a pronoun realizing a finite verb's own person and number, and that a participle in a verbless clause takes only the copula.
The margin's alternative rendering was read and set aside (rule 38).
